prompt:
Vector A has magnitude 8.0 units pointing due east. Vector B has magnitude 6.0 units pointing due north.
(a) State the magnitude and direction of the vector -B. [1]
(b) Calculate the magnitude of the vector difference A - B. [1]

answer.text:
(a) 6.0 units pointing due south.
(b) sqrt(8.0^2 + 6.0^2) = 10 units.

mark_scheme: Part (a) [1 mark]: 6.0 units pointing (due) south (both magnitude and direction required).
Part (b) [1 mark]: 10 units (or 10.0 units) from sqrt(8.0^2 + 6.0^2).
hints: -B has the same magnitude as B but the opposite direction.
A - B is the vector sum of A (east) and -B (south).
solution:
(a) -B has magnitude 6.0 units pointing due south.
(b) |A - B| = sqrt(8.0^2 + 6.0^2) = sqrt(64 + 36) = sqrt(100) = 10 units.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: For (a), reverse direction of B from north to south while keeping magnitude 6.0 units (1 mark).
Step 2: For (b), add A (8.0 east) and -B (6.0 south) using Pythagoras: sqrt(8^2 + 6^2) = 10 units (1 mark).
lesson_anchors: Subtracting vectors means reversing the subtracted vector

abstract_patterns: resolving vectors into perpendicular components and vector addition/subtraction
provenance.independence_statement: Authored independently based on standard Cambridge AS Physics syllabus methods for vector resolution and addition.
